U.S. high school students in grades 9–12 who submit an essay about an eligible elected official's act of political courage, follow the contest's citation rules, and name a nominating teacher.

For musicians with disabilities, ages 14-25, who perform any instrument, voice, or genre.

U.S. citizens in their first three college years with a 2.7+ GPA who enroll full time in a campus-based U.S. degree and have at least one parent from a named Southern Italian region; UNICO membership is not required.
Full-time high school seniors and college/graduate students of Armenian descent who demonstrate financial need.

U.S. citizens or permanent residents who are current high school seniors entering their first undergraduate year and are first-generation college students, meaning their parents or guardians did not complete a bachelor's degree; no Asian American, Pacific Islander, or Chinese identity requirement is stated.
Undergraduate students of Vietnamese American descent, who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and have not yet earned a bachelor's degree.

College-bound and current college, university, or technical-school students in the program's U.S., Indian-citizen, and nonresident-Indian applicant categories, selected through academics, leadership, essays, recommendations, and—for designated awards—financial need.

Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) members pursuing their first associate's or bachelor's degree full-time at a U.S. college.

College juniors, seniors, or master's students studying horticulture, landscape design, floral design, or environmental fields with at least a 3.25 GPA.
Undergraduate sophomores, juniors, or seniors majoring in biology, horticulture, or a related field who want hands-on plant conservation experience at a botanic garden.
U.S. citizen undergraduate sophomores studying environmental, biological, physical, or social sciences relevant to NOAA's mission.
Undergraduate or graduate students studying water-related fields, with preference given to those who are economically disadvantaged.

Adult learners age 19 or older with a high school diploma or GED who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, demonstrate financial need, have not received a prior Imagine America award, enroll at a participating career college, and complete the required assessment and financial-planning video.

U.S. citizens who are formerly incarcerated women or girls, or daughters of incarcerated women, enrolled in or accepted to an accredited undergraduate, graduate, or vocational program; currently incarcerated applicants and students in their final program semester are ineligible.

College sophomores or rising juniors—including eligible two-year students transferring—who plan full-time junior-year study at an accredited four-year U.S. institution and demonstrate commitment to public service.

Active duty, reserve, retired, or auxiliary Coast Guard members, PHS officers serving with the Coast Guard, and their spouses or dependents.

Military spouses (including spouses of the fallen) and caregivers of wounded, ill, or injured post-9/11 service members.
High school seniors, architecture students, community college transfer students, and eligible pre-professional graduates pursuing a NAAB-accredited architecture degree.

Eligible full-time sophomores, juniors, and seniors at four-year U.S. colleges who complete the annual case study in design, merchandising, marketing, analytics, or supply chain; students at nonmember schools and F-1 students may compete under the current rules.

First-generation rising juniors or seniors majoring in public relations, journalism, or communications who have at least a 3.0 GPA and attend an accredited four-year institution full time.

Undergraduate or graduate planning students at U.S. institutions who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and hold free APA student membership; applicants need two recommendations and may not have previously received an APA Foundation-administered scholarship or fellowship.

Students—including F-1 and DACA students—who have completed at least one term in an ABFSE-accredited funeral service or mortuary science program; at least one term must remain after the award date to receive a full award.
For undergraduate juniors, seniors, or graduate students studying facility or stadium management, or a related sports management field, with stadium-related experience.

Current high school seniors with financial need pursuing an eligible major (engineering, computer science, computer information systems, law, or business); per the administering organization's current rules, a disability is not a stated requirement despite the program's name — confirm on the official page.

Undergraduate and graduate photojournalism students at U.S. colleges working in still photography, multimedia, or television news video.

HBCU students pursuing music, music business, marketing, or communications degrees, selected by the Recording Academy's Black Music Collective for a scholarship plus mentorship and GRAMMY Week access.

For Pell Grant-eligible undergraduates who want to study or intern abroad as part of their degree — a federal program built specifically to make study abroad affordable for lower-income students.

For students in ADN, BSN, diploma, or accelerated nursing programs — dozens of named scholarships distributed through one application, no service commitment.
Undergraduate, graduate, medical, master's, and doctoral students with a doctor-diagnosed form of arthritis or rheumatic disease who are involved with the Arthritis Foundation or related advocacy.
National Stuttering Association award for people who stutter pursuing higher education, judged on financial need and involvement in stuttering advocacy.

Undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students majoring in or pursuing real estate, appraisal, or land economics, with awards paid directly to the school.
The Club Foundation's award (CMAA's charitable arm) for rising sophomores and up actively pursuing a management career in the private club industry, 2.5+ GPA.

Undergraduate and graduate interior-design students who completed a research project related to wellness and design; ASID membership is not required.
American Advertising Federation award for college sophomores through seniors in advertising, communications, media, marketing, PR, or journalism.
For college students from underserved communities pursuing advertising, communications, media, marketing, journalism, or PR — paid directly to the student's financial aid office.

Children of eligible Home Depot associates in the United States, Canada, or Mexico who are high school seniors or current college freshmen through juniors entering full-time undergraduate or trade study.
First-generation Wingstop team members pursuing a four-year degree, associate degree, or trade certification.
Cracker Barrel employees at every level, from servers to store support staff, and their children — judged on grades, community service, and extracurriculars.

For dependent children of active-duty, reserve, or retired Coast Guard members, paid directly to a college, university, or trade school for up to four years.

For children and spouses of people killed in the September 11 attacks (families of disabled victims who already registered stay eligible, but new registration for them has closed), funded to keep awarding through 2030.

A judged essay award asking how Alzheimer's or another dementia has touched your life — aimed at teens with that experience, including caregivers, though the formal rules don't require a family connection.
